God, before the foundation of the world, when no one had deserved anything, preordained that in the time of grace he would separate some from the lost, and make the just into the unspotted. For if you do good even to enemies, and give cheerfully, you have breadth. And if in these you persevere to the end, you have length. But if you do not do all these things for the heavenly reward, you have not height, and so already neither breadth nor length. For to have height is to think of God, to love God, and to love him freely, to count him your helper, your crowner, and finally your reward, expecting from him nothing other than himself. If you love, love freely. If you truly love, let him whom you love be your reward. And what is the depth of charity, that is, that you may be able to understand the hidden judgment of God, why he gives to this man and not to that; for from the depth of the judgments of God, which we cannot search out and contemplate, proceeds all that we can do. What I can do I see; whence I can I do not see, except that I know it is from God. But why he gives to one and not to another is far beyond me; it is an abyss and a depth. Now therefore charity itself is exercised in good works for the succour of others, and is extended even to enemies, and this is the breadth. Now with long-suffering it bears adversities and perseveres in what it has truly held, and this is the length.
